KO.rationale: Coca-Cola is a high-quality, cash-generative franchise with durable competitive advantages (brand, distribution, pricing power) and a long dividend track record. Q2 2025 showed solid sequential improvement (revenue +12.6% QoQ, EPS +14.3% QoQ) and the latest Q2 2026 earnings beat estimates (EPS $0.97 vs $0.93 est, revenue $13.37B, 5% volume growth, 6% organic revenue growth, guidance raised). However, the stock is trading near the top of its 1-year P/E range (28.4x vs 23.2-29.6x window) and P/B is elevated at 11.5x (vs 9.4-12.0 range). The 3.5% earnings yield is thin relative to 10-year Treasuries at 4.4%, compressing the equity risk premium. Structural headwinds are real: CSD dependence (~69% of volume), spreading sugar taxes, GLP-1 drug adoption, IRS tax dispute ($6B+ potential liability), Mexico excise tax risk, and plastics litigation. The Q2 2026 earnings beat and World Cup-driven guidance raise provide a modest near-term positive, but the stock appears to be pricing in much of the good news at current multiples. Net: solid business, fair-to-slightly-rich valuation, limited upside at this entry point.
